name: Gas + Ice Giants
story: The outer planetary realm — 5 to 30 AU. Two gas giants (Jupiter, Saturn) with hydrogen-helium envelopes thousands of kilometres deep above small rocky cores; two ice giants (Uranus, Neptune) with water/ammonia/methane mantles under thinner gas. Together they hold 99% of all planetary mass in the solar system. Each has its own moon system that reads as a miniature solar system in itself — Jupiter alone has 95 known moons, including four bigger than Pluto.
comparison: Jupiter is 318× more massive than Earth. The four giants together would form a system 25× the diameter of the inner planets combined.
